jurisdiction.venue: U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Georgia, Atlanta

headline: SEC Sues J. Streicher Financial and Michael Hanlon Over Allegedly Depleted $15 Million ‘Non-Depleting Escrow’
deck: Regulators allege the Georgia adviser promised a public-company client 2% monthly returns inside a principal-protected escrow account, then diverted the $15 million into a parent real-estate joint venture and payouts for a failed European project.

street_crime_compare.exec_summary: The SEC filed a civil complaint in N.D. Ga. alleging Michael P. Hanlon and J. Streicher Financial, LLC misappropriated $15 million promised to a public company's 'non-depleting escrow account' to fund real-estate ventures and Ponzi-like payouts.
street_crime_compare.street_equivalent: Accepting $150,000 in a locked safe-deposit box with a written promise never to touch the cash, spending it on an unrelated building project, and assuring the owner's auditor the box is still full
street_crime_compare.street_sentence: Civil fraud enforcement seeking disgorgement and penalties; no parallel criminal charges announced in the SEC release

sources.title: SEC Charges Georgia Resident and Related Company with Operating Alleged Fraudulent Investment Advisory Scheme (Litigation Release No. 26695)

interactive_art_spec.caption: The Richard B. Russell Federal Building and United States Courthouse in Atlanta, where the S.E.C. filed civil antifraud charges against Michael P. Hanlon and J. Streicher Financial, LLC.
